title: OA SURPRISE AND IAIJUTSU - the dueling draw doctrine, the -1 surprise modifier with the special-situations scope and the two exceptions
audit_comment: OA round sixty-seven (capture p. 218): the Surprise and Iaijutsu dueling draw doctrine - the -1 surprise modifier with the special-situations scope and the two exceptions, single-pass pins per the Chapter 9 provenance shift

banner.title: OA SURPRISE AND IAIJUTSU, printed capture p. 218 - the dueling draw doctrine round
banner.provenance: pinned from the 2018 print capture - the sole surviving pass from Chapter 9 onward, per the R679 provenance shift. The iaijutsu proficiency grants special opportunities to surprise opponents through the lightning speed of the draw, but the modifier lives only in special situations: the noncombat encounter that suddenly erupts into attack. The printed example walks the kneel-beside negotiation with weapons sheathed - the situation grows tense, the NPC attacks without warning, and surprise rolls are made to see if both sides are prepared. THE MODIFIER: a -1 applied to the surprise die roll of the character WITHOUT the proficiency when only one side is trained; when BOTH are trained the -1 applies to BOTH rolls - the startling speed of the trained weapon into action. THE EXCEPTIONS: no modifier when weapons are already drawn, none when the opponent has reason to expect an attack - the modifier only applies when an otherwise peaceful situation erupts into bloody conflict, especially from an unexpected quarter. The prose codifies per the R431 calculus
banner.sentinel: the gap census after this round: 133 closed, 102 open - the Surprise and Iaijutsu box flips (census 602 -> 603); NEXT - R681: the Initiative Modifiers (capture p. 218), prefix dis (verify free at the landing), audit "R681 OA initiative modifiers audit", include after rules/oaiaijutsu.h

consts.name: diqIaijutsuSurpriseModifier
consts.comment: the iaijutsu surprise modifier - a -1 applied to the surprise die roll of the character WITHOUT the proficiency when the iaijutsu-trained character suddenly draws and attacks, reflecting the startling speed of the trained draw (print capture p. 218)

consts.name: diqIaijutsuBothTrappedCount
consts.comment: the both-trained case - when BOTH characters have iaijutsu proficiency, the -1 modifier applies to BOTH surprise die rolls, the two rolls each carrying the draw-speed penalty (print capture p. 218)

bools.name: diqIaijutsuSpecialSituationsOnly
bools.comment: the scope clause - because of the nature of the skill the modifier only applies in special situations: a character in a noncombat encounter suddenly drawing his weapon to attack (print capture p. 218)

bools.name: diqIaijutsuUntrainedCarriesPenalty
bools.comment: the asymmetric case - if one character has iaijutsu proficiency and the other does not, the -1 modifier applies to the surprise die roll of the character without the proficiency, the trained character escaping unpenalized (print capture p. 218)

bools.name: diqIaijutsuBothSidesRollSurprise
bools.comment: the dueling surprise rolls - when the peaceful situation erupts, surprise rolls are made to see if both sides are prepared, the kneel-beside sheathed-weapons negotiation the printed example (print capture p. 218)

bools.name: diqIaijutsuNilWhenWeaponsDrawn
bools.comment: the drawn-weapons exception - no modifier is applied when weapons are already drawn (print capture p. 218)

bools.name: diqIaijutsuNilWhenAttackExpected
bools.comment: the expected-attack exception - no modifier is applied when the opponent has reason to expect an attack (print capture p. 218)

bools.name: diqIaijutsuPeacefulEruptionOnly
bools.comment: the eruption clause - the iaijutsu modifier only applies when an otherwise peaceful situation erupts into bloody conflict, especially from an unexpected quarter (print capture p. 218)

examples.note: the modifier pins - the -1 iaijutsu surprise modifier and the both-trained case applying it to both rolls
